title: Telemetry retention and audit evidence patterns for private deployments
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:

This document defines recommended telemetry retention windows, sampling strategies, evidence packaging patterns, and operator runbooks for customer-facing private (VPC / on-prem) deployments. It is intended to help Customer Success, Security, and Field Operations meet audit requests and regulatory evidence requirements while balancing cost and privacy.

Scope:
- Private deployments (VPC, dedicated rack, air-gapped) managed via Redwood Private control plane.
- Telemetry types: control-plane audit logs, runtime traces (inference requests/latency), KV-cache change logs, operator actions, and package provenance artifacts.
- Not a replacement for legal counsel; use this as engineering guidance for evidence production.

Goals and SLAs:
- Evidence delivery SLA: 72 hours for standard requests, 48 hours for contracted regulated customers (SOC/FinServ).
- Tamper-evidence: delivered bundles must include signed manifest and integrity hashes (SHA256) and KMS-signed attestations when available.
- Minimal data exposure: only include artifacts scoped to requested tenants/time windows.

Telemetry categories and recommended retention windows (default pattern):

| Category | Examples | Minimal retention | Regulated retention | Rationale |
|----------|----------|-------------------:|---------------------:|----------|
| Control-plane audit logs | API key usage, tenant config changes, operator session start/stop | 90 days | 7 years | Audit trail required for security investigations and regulatory audits |
| Inference request metadata (non-pii) | request_id, model, latency, token counts | 30 days | 2 years | Used for SLA/regression analysis; avoid storing full user content unless contractually required |
| Full request payloads | user prompt, attachments | 7 days (default) | Retain only if customer permits; otherwise redact |
| KV cache mutation logs | model swap events, cache invalidation records | 180 days | 3 years | Needed to reconstruct stateful rollback and forensic snapshots |
| Model artifact provenance | signed model manifests, image digests | Indefinite (archive) | Indefinite (archive) | Required for software supply-chain audits; archive outside of hot telemetry stores |
| Operator CLI/SSH session recordings | operator commands, time | 90 days | 2 years | Operator accountability; must be encrypted and access-restricted |

(Note: values above are guidance. Customers with specific regulatory requirements should negotiate longer windows.)

Sampling and aggregation strategies:
- Continuous retention for control-plane audit logs.
- Rolling window aggregation for inference metrics: keep full granularity for 7 days, hourly aggregates for 30 days, daily aggregates thereafter.
- For high-volume tenants, use frequency-based sampling for raw request bodies (e.g., 1% or deterministic seed-based sampling). Sampled items must carry the same request_id namespace to allow correlation.
- Provide an opt-in per-tenant policy to retain raw request payloads for longer windows when the customer explicitly permits.

Implementation examples (Kubernetes / Fluent-bit / S3 pattern):
- Fluent-bit configuration snippet for routing control-plane logs to S3 with prefix by tenant and day:

fluent-bit config:
[INPUT]
    Name tail
    Path /var/log/redwood/control-plane/*.log
    Tag controlplane.%{tenant_id}

[FILTER]
    Name record_modifier
    Match controlplane.*
    Record tenant_id ${tenant_id}

[OUTPUT]
    Name  s3
    Match controlplane.*
    bucket redwood-private-telemetry
    total_file_size 50M
    s3_key_format /tenant_id/%{tenant_id}/year=%Y/month=%m/day=%d/%H%M%S.json

- Retention lifecycle example (S3 lifecycle rules):
  - Transition: Move to Glacier after 90 days for non-essential telemetry.
  - Expiration: auto-delete after configured retention unless archival flag set.

Evidence bundle pattern (file layout):
- manifest.json (signed SHA256 checksum + KMS signature)
- metadata.yaml (tenant, time-window, contact point, cust-approval-id)
- control-plane/ (tar.gz of filtered control-plane logs)
- telemetry-aggregates/ (metrics CSVs, Prometheus snapshots)
- provenance/ (model manifests, image digests, attestations)
- operator-commands/ (redacted operator sessions)

Packaging and delivery workflow (operator playbook):
1) Receive audit request: record intake in JIRA "EVIDENCE-<tenant>-YYYY" and notify Security and Customer Success.
2) Confirm scope: tenant(s), start/end timestamps, artifact types, and legal approvals.
3) Use evidence-builder CLI to produce a sanitized bundle:
   - example: redwood-evidence-builder --tenant <TENANT_ID> --from 2026-04-01T00:00:00Z --to 2026-04-30T23:59:59Z --types control_plane,inference_metadata,provenance --output /tmp/evidence-EVIDENCE-123
4) Run redwood-evidence-validate /tmp/evidence-EVIDENCE-123 and verify manifest signatures.
5) Deliver via customer-approved channel (SFTP to customer-managed endpoint, signed S3 pre-signed URL with one-time password, or sealed-hand-delivery for regulated customers).
6) Log delivery and confirmation in JIRA and attach manifest and delivery receipt.

Automated evidence-builder behavior and flags:
- --sanitize-pii (default ON): redact fields matching configured classifiers.
- --manifest-signing-key <KMS_KEY_ARN>: use customer or Redwood KMS to sign.
- --max-bundle-size: split archives when > 10GB and produce index file.

Forensic and rollback evidence needs:
- To support zero-data-loss upgrades or transactional model swaps, capture the following for the relevant window: KV-cache mutation logs, model load/unload events, and network topology snapshot. Retain these items in a write-once location (WORM) until the upgrade acceptance window closes.

Access controls and encryption:
- At-rest: all telemetry archives must be encrypted with customer-specific KMS keys where available. Use envelope encryption for large objects.
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ and mutual TLS for customer endpoints.
- Access control: RBAC enforced via Control Plane; evidence artifacts scoped to specific operator/service roles.
- Separation-of-duty: evidence production requires two-person approval for regulated requests (operator + security reviewer).

Proof-of-deletion and retention termination:
- When retention expiration triggers deletion, produce a deletion manifest with object keys and deletion timestamps. Sign the deletion manifest and store it under provenance/deletions/YYYY-MM-DD/ to provide evidence that data was purged.
- For GDPR/DSR requests that require tenant-scoped erasure, ensure cross-references in aggregates are scrubbed and append a sanitized-aggregate manifest.

Cost and storage tradeoffs guidance:
- Hot storage (30–90 days) provides fastest evidence turnaround but increases cost; transition older artifacts to cold archive (Glacier, Coldline).
- Provide customers a retention cost estimator spreadsheet (see Related Pages) to help choose windows during onboarding.

Operator runbook: responding to an audit request (step-by-step):
1) Intake: create evidence ticket and set priority based on contract.
2) Scoping call: invite Customer Success, Security, and Field Ops to confirm artifacts.
3) Run evidence-builder with conservative date ranges and sanitize options.
4) Review bundle with Security reviewer for PII leakage.
5) Obtain signing KMS key and produce signed manifest.
6) Transfer bundle via agreed channel, request encrypted delivery receipt.
7) Post-delivery: mark ticket with artifacts and retention lifecycles that apply; schedule additional archive if required.
8) Audit follow-up: produce a short summary report for the customer describing what was included and how to validate checksums.

Validation and QA checks before delivery:
- Integrity: verify SHA256 checksums for each file and a signed manifest.
- Scope: confirm tenant IDs and timestamp coverage match the request.
- Minimal exposure: ensure --sanitize-pii is ON unless explicit permission is present.
- Provenance: include model/image digests and CI build IDs where model artifacts are involved.

Common pitfalls and mitigations:
- Over-retention of raw payloads: mitigate with strict default 7-day policy and opt-in extensions.
- Missing operator action context: ensure operator CLI logging is correlated with control-plane timestamps.
- Large evidence bundles: split and index archives; prefer pre-signed S3 endpoints for large transfers.

Ownership and contacts:
- Evidence production owner: Field Ops (primary).
- Security reviewer: Security team (secondary approver).
- Customer Success: coordinates customer communication.
- Escalation path: PagerDuty runbook -> Security on-call -> Field Ops lead.

Appendices:
A) Sample manifest.json (truncated)
{
  "tenant": "tenant-123",
  "from": "2026-04-01T00:00:00Z",
  "to": "2026-04-30T23:59:59Z",
  "files": ["control-plane/2026-04-01.log.gz", "provenance/model-manifest.json"],
  "signature": "KMS-SIGNATURE-BASE64"
}

B) Evidence delivery checklist (short):
- [ ] Ticket created and scope confirmed
- [ ] Evidence-builder run and pass validation
- [ ] Manifest signed and verified
- [ ] Delivery channel confirmed and tested
- [ ] Post-delivery confirmation received
